notes.text: Timeline: ~7000 BCE; Event/Ruler: Mehrgarh Civilization; Key Details: One of the earliest farming settlements, located in Balochistan, Pakistan.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Considered a precursor to the Indus Valley Civilization.; How It Ended: Gradual decline as people migrated eastward, contributing to Indus Valley Civilization.

Timeline: ~3300- 1700 BCE; Event/Ruler: Indus Valley Civilization; Key Details: Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro (Pakistan), advanced urban planning, trade, undeciphered script. *Dravidians were the people who founded Harappan Civilization; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: First major civilization in South Asia, known for its sanitation and trade networks.; How It Ended: Likely ended due to drying of rivers, or Aryan migration.

Timeline: ~1500 BCE; Event/Ruler: Aryan Migration; Key Details: Indo-European Aryans came from Central Asia (likely the region near Iran and Southern Russia).; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Introduced Sanskrit, caste system, and Vedic religion to the region.; How It Ended: Integrated into Indian society, evolving into the Vedic Age.

Timeline: 563 BC; Event/Ruler: Birth of Budha; Key Details: Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) was born in present-day Nepal. He was son of King Suddhodana.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: He preached mostly in north India & Nepal.

Timeline: ~600 BCE; Event/Ruler: Mahajanapadas; Key Details: 16 large kingdoms emerged in North India and Pakistan, including Gandhara, Kamboja, etc; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Gandhara (in present-day Pakistan) became an important Buddhist and trade center.; How It Ended: Later absorbed into larger empires like Maurya and Kushan.

Timeline: 326 BCE; Event/Ruler: Alexander the Great's Invasion; Key Details: Defeated King Porus at the Battle of Hydaspes but stopped at the Beas River. Shot by an arrow in the Siege of the Mallian city (Multan, Pakistan).; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Hellenistic influence in Gandhara, Greek satraps in the region.; How It Ended: Alexander's army mutinied, forcing him to return. He later died in Babylon (323 BCE).

Timeline: 321-185 BCE; Event/Ruler: Maurya Empire; Key Details: Capital: Pataliputra (modern- day Patna, India). *Chandragupta defeated the Greeks and spread Budhism via missionaries. *Ashoka promoted Buddhism across the region.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Spread of Buddhism in Gandhara (Pakistan) and Central Asia under Ashoka.; How It Ended: Weak rulers after Ashoka led to the empire's collapse.

Timeline: ~200 BCE - 500 CE; Event/Ruler: Foreign Conquests (Indo-Greeks, Indo-Parthians); Key Details: Greeks and Parthians ruled parts of the Indo-Pak region at different times.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Spread of Greek culture, trade, and Buddhism in Gandhara.; How It Ended: Conquered by local Indian and Persian rulers.

Timeline: 127-375 CE; Event/Ruler: Kushan Empire; Key Details: Capital: Peshawar (Pakistan). *Kanishka was the greatest Kushan ruler, promoting Buddhism and trade.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Connected Indo- Pak region to the Silk Road, boosting trade & culture.; How It Ended: Kushan Empire weakened by internal conflicts, fell to the Sassanid Persians and Gupta Empire.

Timeline: ~500 BCE - 600 CE; Event/Ruler: Gandhara Civilization; Key Details: Capital: Taxila (Pakistan). Located in NW Pakistan & Afghanistan, influenced by Greek, Persian, and Buddhist cultures.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Became a center for Gandhara art (Greco-Buddhist style).; How It Ended: Declined after Hindu rulers & later Islamic invasions.

Timeline: ~450- 600 CE; Event/Ruler: Hepthalite Huns (White Huns); Key Details: Nomadic invaders from Central Asia (likely Mongolia/Tajikistan), attacked India, Persia, and Gandhara.; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Destroyed Buddhist monasteries, killed monks, and ended Buddhism in Gandhara.; How It Ended: Defeated by Persians and Indian rulers

Timeline: 712 CE; Event/Ruler: Raja Dahir (Sindh's Last Hindu King); Key Details: Fought against Muhammad bin Qasim in the Battle of Aror (near modern Rohri, Sindh).; Impact on Indo- Pak Region: Start of Islamic rule in the Indo- Pak region.; How It Ended: Killed in battle; Muhammad bin Qasim established Islamic rule in Sindh.

Samanid Dynasty rules Central Asia, Iran, and Afghanistan - Relied on Turkic slave generals.; Event: Alp Tigin establishes independent rule in Ghazna; Key Figures & Designations: Alp Tigin (Former Samanid General, Founder of Ghaznavid rule in Ghazna); Outcome/Impact: Broke away from the Samanids and established control over Ghazna (modern-day Ghazni, Afghanistan).

Event: Sabuktigin becomes ruler of Ghazna; Key Figures & Designations: Sabuktigin (Son-in-law of Alp Tigin, Ruler of Ghazna, Known as Founder of ''Ghaznavid Dynasty''); Outcome/Impact: Expanded Ghaznavid control over Kabul and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Event: Hindu Shahi Dynasty ruled Gandhara, Kabul Valley, Punjab; Key Figures & Designations: Jayapala (Hindu Shahi King), Anandapala (his son & successor); Outcome/Impact: Hindu Shahis controlled Gandhara (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan), Kabul Valley, Punjab, and parts of Kashmir.

Year: 1000 CE; Event: First raid by Mahmud of Ghazni; Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni (Sultan of Ghazni); Outcome/Impact: Border regions of Hindustan (In modern day Pakistan and Afghanistan) marking the first invasion into the Indian subcontinent.

Year: 1001 CE; Event: Battle of Peshawar; Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni vs. Jayapala (Hindu Shahi King); Outcome/Impact: Jayapala defeated and captured, later released. Due to humiliation, he committed self-immolation in 1002 CE.

Year: 1008 CE; Event: Battle of Waihind; Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni vs. Anandapala (Son of Jayapala); Outcome/Impact: Anandapala defeated, Ghaznavid control extended over Punjab and Gandhara.
Year: 1025 CE; Event: Plunder of Somnath Temple; Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni; Outcome/Impact: Somnath Temple (Gujarat, India) was looted, its idol destroyed.
Year: 1026 CE; Event: End of Hindu Shahi Dynasty; Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni; Outcome/Impact: The last Hindu Shahi ruler was defeated, marking the end of the dynasty.

Year: 1027 CE; Event: Last raid by Mahmud of Ghazni (Jats of Sindh); Key Figures & Designations: Mahmud of Ghazni; Outcome/Impact: Final raid targeted the Jats of Sindh, marking Mahmud's last expedition to India.
Year: 1030 CE; Event: Death of Mahmud of Ghazni; Key Figures & Designations: Mas'ud I (Son of Mahmud, Ghaznavid Sultan); Outcome/Impact: Internal conflicts weakened Ghaznavid rule.

Year: 1099 CE; Event: Decline of Ghaznavids due to Seljuk pressure; Key Figures & Designations: Seljuk Empire, Ghaznavid rulers; Outcome/Impact: Seljuks pushed Ghaznavids out of Khorasan, reducing their power.
Year: 1151 CE; Event: Ghaznavids lose Ghazni to Ghurids; Outcome/Impact: Ghurids sacked Ghazni, forcing Ghaznavid rulers to retreat to Lahore.

Year: 1186 CE; Event: Fall of the Ghaznavid Empire; Key Figures & Designations: Khusrau Malik (Last Ghaznavid Sultan), Muhammad of Ghor (Shahāb-ud-Din Muhammad Ghouri) (Ghurid Ruler); Outcome/Impact: Ghurids captured Lahore, marking the end of the Ghaznavid Empire.

Year: 1191 CE; Event: First Battle of Tarain; Key Figures: Muhammad Ghori vs. Prithviraj Chauhan (Ruler of a small Rajput state in North India, centered in Ajmer & Delhi); Outcome/Impact: Ghori defeated and forced to retreat. (Fought in present-day Haryana, India)

Year: 1192 CE; Event: Second Battle of Tarain; Key Figures: Muhammad Ghori vs. Prithviraj Chauhan; Outcome/Impact: Prithviraj defeated and captured; Delhi & Ajmer came under Muslim rule. (Fought in present-day Haryana, India)

Year: 1194 CE; Event: Battle of Chandawar; Key Figures: Muhammad Ghori vs. Jaichand (Ruler of Kannauj, a small kingdom in North India); Outcome/Impact: Jaichand defeated, securing Ghurid control over North India. (Fought in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India)

Year: 1206 CE; Event: Assassination of Muhammad Ghori; Key Figures: Muhammad Ghori, Qutb-ud-din Aibak (His slave general & founder of the Delhi Sultanate); Outcome/Impact: Ghori assassinated near the Jhelum River; Aibak became the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

Dynasty: Mamluk (Slave); Start Year: 1206; End Year: 1290; First King: Qutb- ud-din Aibak; Last King: Muiz-ud-din Muhammad Qaiqabad; Formation: Established by Qutb-ud-din Aibak after Muhammad Ghori's death.; Decline: Overthrown by Jalal-ud-din Khilji in 1290.; Origin & Ethnicity: Turkic (Central Asia) - Former slaves (Mamluks) of Ghori.

Dynasty: Khilji; Start Year: 1290; End Year: 1320; First King: Jalal-ud- din Khilji; Last King: Khusrau Khan; Formation: Jalal-ud-din Khilji took power by overthrowing the Mamluks.; Decline: Khusrau Khan was overthrown by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq.; Origin & Ethnicity: Turk-Afghan origin (Khalaj tribe, Afghanistan).

Dynasty: Tughlaq; Start Year: 1320; End Year: 1414; First King: Ghiyas- ud-din Tughlaq; Last King: Nasir-ud-din Mahmud; Formation: Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq overthrew Khusrau Khan.; Decline: Weakened by Timur's invasion (1398), finally ended by the Sayyids.; Origin & Ethnicity: Turkic (Central Asia & Persian influences).

Dynasty: Sayyid; Start Year: 1414; End Year: 1451; First King: Khizr Khan; Last King: Ala-ud-din Alam Shah; Formation: Khizr Khan, a former Tughlaq governor, took power after Timur's invasion.; Decline: Ala-ud-din Alam Shah abdicated, power taken by Bahlul Lodi.; Origin & Ethnicity: Claimed Arab descent (Sayyids, descendants of Prophet Muhammad).

Dynasty: Lodi; Start Year: 1451; End Year: 1526; First King: Bahlul Lodi; Last King: Ibrahim Lodi; Formation: Bahlul Lodi overthrew the Sayyids and became Sultan.; Decline: Defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526), marking the start of the Mughal Empire.; Origin & Ethnicity: Afghan (Pashtun, Lodi tribe).

Qutb-ud-din Aibak - Founded the Delhi Sultanate after Ghori's death.; Capital: Lahore (later shifted to Delhi by Iltutmish).; Started Qutb Minar in Delhi (1199), as General of Shahbudin Ghauri; Built Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque (Delhi,1193) as General of Shahbudin Ghauri, the first mosque in India.; Patronized Sufi saint Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (born Fergana Valley, modern Uzbekistan).; Known as Lakh Baksh (giver of lakhs).; Died falling from a horse in Lahore while playing polo.

Iltutmish (1211- 1236) - Son in law & Slave of Aibak; Shifted capital to Delhi from Lahore.; Introduced the Iqta System - a revenue system where nobles (Iqtadars) collected taxes in exchange for military and administrative duties.; Introduced Silver Tanka & Copper Jital currency:; Stabilized the economy, standardized trade, and reduced barter system.; The silver coin (Tanka) became a model for later Indian currencies.; Completed Qutb Minar (Delhi,1229).; Declared Delhi as the permanent capital.; Important Contributions: Formed the Chahalgani (Group of Forty) - a council of 40 powerful Turkish nobles to assist in governance.

Razia Sultana (1236-1240) - Daughter of Iltutmish; First and only female Sultan of Delhi.; Faced opposition from Turkish nobles (Chahalgani group).; Promoted merit-based governance over hereditary rule.; Appointed Abyssinian Malik Yakut as key official.; Led armies herself and dressed like a man in battle.; Deposed and killed in a rebellion.

Ghiyas-ud-din Balban - Former Slave of Iltutmish; Introduced Theory of Kingship (divine authority of Sultan).; Declared himself "Zill-e-Ilahi" (Shadow of God) to justify absolute monarchy.; Enforced Sajdah (prostration) & Paibos (kissing Sultan's feet) in court.; Strengthened centralized rule and crushed rebellions.; Abolished the Chahalgani to end noble interference.

Jalal-ud-din Khilji - Overthrew and killed Sultan Kayqubad (last Mamluk ruler) to establish the Khilji dynasty.; Adopted a mild and lenient rule to gain legitimacy.; Assassinated by his nephew Alauddin Khilji.

Sultan: Alauddin Khilji; Reign: 1296- 1316; Important Contributions: Was uneducated but had strong administrative and military skills.; Expanded the Delhi Sultanate through military campaigns; Introduced price control and market reforms.; Abolished the Iqtadari system to centralize revenue collection.; Stored large quantities of food grains in government granaries to regulate supply and fight famines.; Given the title Sikandar-e-Sani (Second Alexander).
Qutb-ud-din Mubarak Shah - Revoked Alauddin's strict policies.; Promoted art and culture.; Assassinated by his favorite, Khusro Khan.
Khusro Khan - First and only non-Turkic ruler of the dynasty.; Overthrown and killed by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq.

Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq - Founded the Tughlaq dynasty after overthrowing Khusro Khan.; Strengthened military and administrative systems.; Built Tughlaqabad Fort in Delhi.; Assassinated by his son Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

Muhammad bin Tughlaq - Highly educated but impractical in governance.; Known as the Mad King; Shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (originally called Devagiri), causing hardship.; Introduced token currency (copper coins), which failed due to forgery.; Attempted agricultural reforms: increased land tax, granted loans, and expanded cultivation, but these failed due to excessive taxation, lack of irrigation, and famine.; Expanded the empire to its largest extent but struggled with administration.; Faced multiple rebellions due to harsh policies (inhumane punishments)

Firoz Shah Tughlaq - Promoted welfare projects such as canals, gardens, and hospitals.; Imposed Jizyah on Brahmins.; Built Firoz Shah Kotla (fort in Delhi) and repaired Qutub Minar.; Established Jaunpur city in UP, Firuzpur in Punjab.; Reduced harsh punishments and imposed lower taxes.; Established 1200+ fruit gardens.

Mahmud Tughlaq - Last ruler of the dynasty, weak and ineffective.; Faced Timur's invasion in 1398, which devastated Delhi.; Could not control regional governors, leading to the collapse of the dynasty.

Khizr Khan - Founded the Sayyid dynasty after Timur's invasion weakened the Tughlaq rule.; Did not assume the title of Sultan and ruled as Timur's vassal; Focused on restoring order in Delhi.; Collected taxes on behalf of the Timurids.
Ala-ud-din Alam Shah - Last Sayyid ruler; weak and ineffective.; Abandoned Delhi in 1448 and shifted to Badaun (City in UP).; Surrendered Delhi to Bahlul Lodi, marking the end of the dynasty.

Sultan: Bahlul Lodi; Reign: 1451- 1489; Important Contributions: Founder of the Lodi dynasty after overthrowing the Sayyids.; Strengthened the Afghan rule in India.; Encouraged Afghan nobles to settle in India.

Sultan: Ibrahim Lodi; Reign: 1517- 1526; Important Contributions: Last Lodi ruler; faced internal revolts and noble rebellions.; Lost the loyalty of Afghan chiefs due to his autocratic rule.; Defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (In Haryana) (1526), marking the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

Emperor: Babur; Reign: 1526-1530; Notable Aspects: Founder of the Mughal Empire.; Was from Fergana, Uzbekistan.; Defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526).; Introduced gunpowder and artillery in India.; Wrote his autobiography BaburNama in Turkic.; Buried in Kabul

Emperor: Akbar; Reign: 1556-1605; Notable Aspects: Expanded the empire significantly.; Won Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu Baikal.; Secular policies: (- Abolished Jizya tax. - Introduced Sulh-i-Kul (peace for all religions). - Held religious debates at Ibadat Khana. - Started Din-i-Ilahi (1582). -Captured Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi in - Appointed Hindus to high administrative posts. - Banned cow slaughter); Introduced Mansabdari system (rank-based military, civil administration). *Naqdi or Land to each officer for service. Led to Feudalism.; Shifted capital to Fatehpur Sikri (1571-1585) (In District Agra today), then back to Agra.; Built Fatehpur Sikri (1571-1585); Buried in Akbar's Tomb, Agra

Emperor: Jahangir; Reign: 1605-1627; Notable Aspects: Issued "Chain of Justice" at Agra Fort for public grievances.; Patronized art and painting, encouraged Persian-style miniatures.; Married Mehr-un-Nisa (Nur Jahan), who became politically influential.; Buried in Jahangir's Tomb, Lahore

Emperor: Shah Jahan; Reign: 1628-1658; Notable Aspects: Golden Age of Mughal architecture.; Built Taj Mahal & Shalimar Gardens for wife Mumtaz Mahal.; Overthrown by Aurangzeb in 1658, imprisoned in Agra Fort until death (1666).
Emperor: Aurangzeb; Reign: 1658-1707; Notable Aspects: Empire reached its greatest territorial extent.; Won Battle of Deorai (1659) against Dara Shikoh.; Reimposed Jizya tax

Emperor: Muhammad Shah Rangeela; Reign: 1719 - 1748; Major Aspects: Indulgent and pleasure-seeking ruler; focused on luxury rather than governance.; Faced the 1739 invasion of Delhi by Nadir Shah, who plundered the city.; Lost the Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond to Nadir Shah.; The empire weakened as regional rulers gained autonomy.

Emperor: Shah Alam II; Reign: t 1760 -; 1806; Major Aspects: Faced the 1761 invasion by Ahmad Shah Abdali, who defeated he Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat and plundered Delhi. Defeated in the Battle of Buxar (1764) by the British, losing effective control. Blinded in 1788 by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla (A local Afghan Warlord).

Emperor: Bahadur Shah II (Zafar); Reign: 1837 - 1857; Major Aspects: Last Mughal emperor; more of a poet than a ruler. Became the symbolic leader of the Revolt of 1857, but had no real power. After the British crushed the revolt, he was captured and exiled to Rangoon (Burma). The Mughal dynasty officially ended with his exile.

Sir Syed Ahmed Khan - Born: 1817, Delhi; Entered the service of East India Company in 1838; Became judge: 1846; Gulshan School in Muradabad (1859), Victoria School in Ghazipur (1863); Scientific Society: 1864 (Ghazipur); MAO School Aligarh 1875; MAO College Aligarh 1877; First secretary of the Board of Trustees of Aligarh College; College became Aligarh Muslim University: 1920 (King George V allowed it); Two-Nation Theory idea: 1887; Magazines: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq; Books: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind, Asrar ul Sanadeed, Ahkam-e-Ta'am wa Ahl-e Kitab, Khutbat e Ahmdiya (In response of Life of Muhammad By William Muir); Joined ILC: 1878; Information: Died in 1898

Syed Ahmed Shaheed Barelvi - Born: 1786, Rae Bareli (UP); Partner in Jihad: Shah Ismail Shaheed; Started Jihad Movement: 1826; Initial Jihad: Peshawar region; Fought against Sikh rule; Died: 1831, Battle of Balakot (Along with Shah Ismail grand son of Shah Wali Ullah)

Maulana Zafar Ali Khan - Editor of Zamindar (Newspaper was started in 1903 from Lahore by his father Maulana Sirajuddin Ahmed) Later restarted from Lahore in 1911 by him after his father death

Maulana Muhammad Ali Johar - Educated at Aligarh Muslim University and later at Oxford University (England); Prominent leader of Khilafat Movement along with his brother Shaukat Ali; One of the founders of the All India Muslim League (1906); Editor and founder of the famous newspaper "The Comrade" (English) - started in 1911; Also launched Urdu newspaper "Hamdard"; Represented Indian Muslims at the Round Table Conference (1930); Died in 1931 in London, buried in Jerusalem (as per his wish: "bury me in a free land")

Syed Ameer Ali - Born: Bengal; Book: Spirit of Islam, History of Saracens; Founded National Muhammadan Association: 1877; Established London branch of Muslim League: 1908; First Muslim judge in British Privy Council
Sir Agha Khan III - Born: Karachi; First President of Muslim League (1906); Led Simla Deputation: 1906; Promoted education via Aligarh Movement; Represented Muslims in Round Table Conferences

Allama Iqbal - Born: 1877, Sialkot; BA: Government College Lahore; MA Philosophy; Inspiration from Jalal-uddin Rumi.; Influenced by the teachings of Sir Thomas Arnold, his philosophy teacher at Government College Lahore; In 1905, he travelled to England for that purpose.; Got BA from Cambridge in 1906; Called to Bar in 1906 at Lincloln's Inn; Moved to Germany in 1907 for PHD; PhD from Munich University: 1908 (Development of Metaphysics in Persia); Joined Muslim League: 1908; Allahabad Address: 1930; Books: Bang-e-Dra, Bal-e-Jibril, Zarb-e-Kaleem, Payam-e-Mashriq, Rumooz-e-Bekhudi, Asrar-e-Khudi; Lectures Book: Reconstruction of Religious thought in Islam; Died: 1938, Lahore

Muhammad Ali Jinnah - Born: 25 Dec 1876, Karachi; Father: Poonja Jinnah; Mother: Mithibai; First Marriage: Emibai (1892) - died soon; Second Marriage: Ruttie (Rattan) Bai (1918); Went to UK: 1892, studied Law at Lincoln's Inn, Returned: 1896; In 1895, at age 19, he became the youngest British Indian to be called to the bar in England.; Joined Congress: 1906 - Joined Muslim League: 1913; Became League President: 1916; Information: Left India: 1931, settled in London - Returned: 1934; Launched the DAWN newspaper in Delhi & Karachi in 1941; Died: 11 Sep 1948, Karachi

Darul Uloom Deoband - Founded in 1866 in Deoband, Saharanpur (UP, India); Founders: Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautvi; Aim: To revive Islamic values and oppose British influence; Focused on pure Islamic education (Dars-e-Nizami curriculum); Followed Hanafi school of thought; Actively participated in Khilafat Movement and non-cooperation movement; Opposed Western-style education; Published religious journal "Al-Qasim"

Nadwat-ul-Ulama - Organization of Ulemas named nadwat ul Ulema was established in 1892 in Kanpur at Madrassa Faiz e Aam.; Founder: Muhammad Ali Mungeri; Later they formed a Madrassa in 1898, named Dar ul Uloom Nadwat-ul-Ulema in Lucknow, UP; Aimed to modernize traditional Islamic education; Tried to unite different sects and schools of thought; Curriculum included both Islamic and modern subjects; First principal: Shibli Nomani; Journal: "Al-Nadwah"

Sindh Madressatul Islam - Founded in 1885 in Karachi; Founder: Hassan Ali Effendi; Inspired by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan's Aligarh model; Purpose: Spread modern education among Sindhi Muslims; Provided both religious and contemporary education; Famous Alumni: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah; Played an important role in Muslim awakening in Sindh; Jinnah studied here at age in 1887.; Upgraded to Sindh Madressatul Islam University in 2012

Islamia College Peshawar - Founded in 1913 in Peshawar; Founders: Nawab Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Khan; Details / Notes: Inspired by Aligarh Movement; Aim: Provide quality education to Pashtun Muslims; Major center of Pakistan Movement activities in NWFP; Quaid-e-Azam visited multiple times, praised its role; Later affiliated with University of Peshawar

Government of India Act (1858) - Abolition of the East India Company; British Crown took direct control of India (1858).; Queen Victoria declared Empress of India (Kaiser-e-Hind) (1877).; Introduction of the Viceroy system for British governance in India.
Indian Councils Act (1861) - Introduced limited representation for Indians in some provinces.

Urdu-Hindi Controversy (1867) - Started in 1867 in Banaras.; Debate over replacing Urdu (Nasta'leeq) with Hindi (Devanagari script) as the official court language.; Syed Ahmad Khan warned it could divide Hindus and Muslims.

Arya Samaj Movement (1875) - Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay.; Aimed to promote Vedic teachings and reform Hindu society.; It promoted Shuddhi Movement (reconversion of Muslims and Christians to Hinduism).

Formation of Indian National Congress (1885) - Founded by A.O. Hume, a retired British officer.; Formed in Bombay (Mumbai) with its headquarters in Allahabad.; Aimed to demand political reforms and greater Indian representation in governance.
Indian Councils Act (1892) - Number of Indian members increased in Legislative Councils.; Members could ask questions (but not discuss or criticize policies).

Urdu-Hindi Controversy (1900) - Ordered by Lieutenant Governor of United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh) by Sir Anthony MacDonnell; Allow Hindi alongside Urdu as the official language in courts and offices.

Partition of Bengal (1905) - British divided Bengal into East Bengal (Muslim majority) and West Bengal (Hindu majority).; By Lord Curzon; East Bengal and Assam were merged and Dhaka was made its capital; West Bengal was merged with Bihar and Orissa, with Calcutta as its capital

Simla Deputation (1906) - Muslim leaders, led by Aga Khan, met Lord Minto in Shimla (1906), demanding separate electorates for Muslims.; Total 35 men; British accepted their demand, recognizing Muslims as a separate political entity.
Formation of Muslim League (1906) - Founded on: 30th December 1906 in Dhaka; Formed by: Nawab Salimullah; First President: Sir Aga Khan

Second President: Raja Sahib of Mahmoodabad (1910); First Session in Karachi in 1907; England Branch: Founded in 1908 by Syed Ameer Ali; Iqbal Joined: 1908; Jinnah Joined: 1913; Liaquat Ali Khan Joined: 1923; Fatima Jinnah Joined: 1937; Jinnah Became Head (President): 1916; Aim was to protect Muslim political rights and promote loyalty to the British government.
Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908) - Started in 1905 against the Partition of Bengal; Promoted boycott of British goods; Led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Rabindranath Tagore

Minto-Morley Reforms (1909) - Introduced by Lord Minto (Viceroy of India) and John Morley (Secretary of State for India); Granted separate electorates to Muslims for the first time.; Increased the number of Indian members in Legislative Councils.
Annulment of Bengal (1911) - Partition of Bengal (1905) was cancelled by British due to Hindu protests.; Done by Lord Hardinge; Announced by King George V during the Delhi Durbar.

Kanpur Mosque Tragedy (1913) - Occurred in Kanpur during the demolition of a mosque near the; For road widening, sparking Muslim protests.; Police opened fire on protesting Muslims, killing hundreds of Muslims.

Lucknow Pact (1916) - Agreement between Muslim League and Congress in Lucknow.; Jinnah (Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity) - title given by Sarojini Naidu.; Headed by Bal Gangadhar Tilak from Hindus.; Granted separate electorates and one-third seats to Muslims.; System of Weightage (Muslims were given more seats than their population in minority provinces (like UP and Bihar). Muslims were given less seats than their population in majority provinces (like Punjab and Bengal))

Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) - Started by Ali Brothers (Maulana Shaukat Ali & Maulana Muhammad Ali Johar) to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.; Tark-e-Mawalat (Boycott of British Goods) began in 1920 by Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind.; Linked with Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922).; Many Muslims migrated to Afghanistan during the Hijrat Movement (1920) but returned disappointed.; Gandhi left the movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident (violent protest).
Ended in 1924 when the Ottoman Caliphate was abolished by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

Rowlatt Act (1919) - Introduced by Sir Sidney Rowlatt to suppress revolutionary activities.; Allowed the British government to arrest anyone without trial or warrant for up to 2 years.; Known as the Black Act by Indians due to its oppressive nature.

Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919) - Happened on 13th April 1919 in Amritsar, Punjab during Baisakhi festival.; Ordered by General Dyer, who fired on unarmed civilians protesting against the Rowlatt Act.; Around 1000 people killed and 1500 injured.
Jinnah Left Legislative Council (1919) - Reason: To protest against the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre.; He called the Rowlatt Act "a law of oppression and injustice".

Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) - Introduced through the Government of India Act 1919 by Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy) and Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State of India); Introduced the system of Dyarchy (dual government) in provinces, dividing subjects into Transferred (handled by Indians) and Reserved (controlled by British).; Provided separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, and Anglo-Indians.

Jinnah Left Congress (1920) - Reason: He opposed Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement; Jinnah believed in constitutional struggle, while Gandhi promoted civil disobedience and mass protests. * He had joined congress in 1906

Chaura Chauri Incident (1922) - Happened in 1922 in Chauri Chaura, Uttar Pradesh.; Angry protestors set a police station on fire, killing 22 policemen during the Non-Cooperation Movement.; The protest turned violent, which was against Gandhi's policy of non- violence.

Simon Commission (1927) - Sent by the British Government to review the Government of India Act 1919 and suggest reforms.; Headed by Sir John Simon with all seven members British (no Indian member).; Announced: 1927; Came to India:1928; Report Presented: 1930; Called for abolishment of Dyarchy system in provinces
Protests led to killing of Lala Lajpat Rai (Congress leader)

Delhi Proposals (1927) - Presented by Jinnah; Muslims will give up demand of separate electroates if Sindh is separated from Bombay and NWFP, Balcohistan be given full provincial status.; One-third representation for Muslims in Central Legislature.

2nd Round Table Conference (1931) - Attended by Gandhi (Congress); Attended by both Jinnah and Iqbal

*All three round table conferences happened in London. Headed by British PM Ramsay MacDonald. Muslim League delegation was led by Agha Khan III.
